kernel_pair.source: CIF_v2 v2.1.0 Pairing (byte-frozen, opencif/reference); Hill fit: glossary macros

reasons: the drawn parts collide: 'inlet and head' and 'leg 2' are 0.0 um apart (they overlap; they must keep the 20.0 um process floor).  Remedies: move 'inlet and head' and 'leg 2' apart until at least the 20.0 um floor separates them (they overlap now); the layout uses the spec's layout.leg_spacing_um = 818 as given; the generator's own rule spaces this paperclip's legs 1668 um apart (max(2 x 409, 1109 + 409) + 150 um: the widest row's half-width and the head's); give no spacing to use it, or space the legs beside the head at least that far; or change the parts themselves (a narrower head, smaller ports, another leg count or layout)

P8.status: diagnostic only, not an audit and not gated (docs/LIMITATIONS.md 6): the two criteria of CIF_v2's physics auditor check P8, computed from the design (CIF_v2's auditor is not run on the exported mask; opencif's own drawn-mask checks are assessment.status.drawn_mask_assessment) at the auditor's default operating point (5 uL/min) and at the design flow; its 0.05 Re D_h is the entrance length spec v5, the glossary and CIF_v2 S16-c call wrong in this regime, and its Re limit 1.0 is CIF_v2's settable default (App. B prints no value), not the design envelope's (Re_max = 10, M14)

gates.dean_note: no bound: the channel Reynolds bound 2 rho Q/(mu (h + F_min - 0.1 um)) = 10.01 exceeds 10 (the gated centre-channel Re is Re_max)

shear_peak.formula: C(alpha) Q_c / (a b^2), the centre flow entering each row, on the planned centre widths at the operating flow (spec v5 S16-b, S:449)
shear_peak.note_rows: every row's peak falls with its centre flow once the centre is at its floor (or constant)

fluid.note: water (the default); the Reynolds gates scale with rho/mu; the schedule does not depend on the fluid (resistance ratios, Newtonian); the absolute resistances in the record (Pa s/m^3) are at water's viscosity

gates.plateau_all_planned_rows_note: rc7: planned row cutoffs over the centre width, declared rows included, over the rows extracting at least 5 % of the constant-cutoff fraction at their width; the share is of the flow all rows extract

cutoff_band_um.basis: on the plateau: the kappa_g interval x delta*
cutoff_band_um.method: on the plateau (u_min >= 0.035): the kappa_g interval x delta*.  Below it the record uses App. B P-C7.1 (the frozen Hill fit; glossary \hillKmax, \hillUhalf, \hillN): band [kappa(u) delta*, kappa_g delta*], plateau-anchored (App. B C7 CQ3)

refused.advice: the parts of the drawn outline (the inlet with the head, each leg, each U-turn, the outlet) must keep the process floor from every part they are not joined to, with the outlet ports separated and at least 2 mm from the inlet port; no photomask is written for an outline that does not (the remedies are named above).

collisions: 'inlet and head' and 'leg 2' are 0.0 um apart (they overlap; they must keep the 20.0 um process floor)

notes: measured on the drawing: every side segment, head unit length and width, U-turn side and centre arc, outlet lead, gap opening and centre width.  Taken from the design (not measured): the post length across the flow (gap length l_g) and so the side channels' inner edge, the radii of the head and outlet arcs (their widths are measured), the head rows' centre-path lengths, and any off-chip tubing.
